content: KLK9, also known as kallikrein-related peptidase 9, is an enzyme encoded by the KLK9 gene in humans. KLK9 is a member of the kallikrein subgroup of serine proteases, which are enzymes with a wide range of physiological roles across various tissues. This enzyme is predominantly expressed in the thymus, testis, spinal cord, cerebellum, trachea, mammary gland, prostate, brain, salivary gland, ovary, and skin. In terms of clinical significance, KLK9 is regulated by steroid hormones in ovarian and breast cancer cell lines. It has been identified as a potential prognostic biomarker for patients with early-stage ovarian and breast cancers. Additionally, the excretion of KLK9 in urine has been linked to cardiac hypertrophy, increased aortic wall thickness, and certain renal alterations.
